tableau-zebre.description_html:
Zebra wall art gives a wall what few patterns can: rhythm, contrast and instant elegance. Our collection brings together canvases selected and retouched by hand by our creative studio in Toulouse: photography-inspired black and white pieces (the wild gaze, a majestic zebra against a dark background, a zebra in the snow), colourful and rainbow zebras in a pop art spirit, tribal patterns in copper ochres, an African mother and child, street art, and watercolour for a child's room.

Each piece is printed to order in Europe on 285 g/m² polyester canvas, with high-pigment inks guaranteed for 75 years, then stretched by hand over a solid wood stretcher 3 cm (1.2 in) deep. Sizes run from 30 × 40 to 90 × 120 cm (11.8 × 15.7 to 35.4 × 47.2 in), and up to 100 × 100 cm (39.4 × 39.4 in) for square artworks, with five edge finishes and an optional frame. In the living room above the sofa, in a bedroom, an entryway or a home office, the zebra suits every style. Free delivery.

tableau-zebre.guide:
Zebra wall art: a pattern that shapes the wall

Some walls have been waiting a long time. You sense something is missing, without quite knowing what. Often, the answer lies in a few bold lines: those of the zebra. Its stripes sketch an architecture all on their own; they guide the eye, give rhythm to the space and bring that black and white contrast that goes with almost everything, along with a breath of the African savannah. A zebra painting gives a wall a line, a rhythm, a presence.

At MyselfMonArt, a creative studio founded in Toulouse in 2022, every artwork is selected and then retouched by hand by our art direction team: the depth of the blacks, the fine detail of the coat, the accuracy of the colours. Nothing enters the collection by chance, and it is this care you will find once the canvas is hanging in your home.

Which zebra wall art should you choose?

It all begins with the atmosphere you want to create. Our collection unfolds in four families.

Black and white zebra wall art, a timeless choice

This is the choice that outlasts trends and house moves alike. The wild gaze in black and white plays on a hypnotic close-up, right up to the eye and the stripes. The majestic zebra on a black background sculpts the light like a studio portrait, with its golden highlights. And the zebra in the winter snow tells the story of an unexpected encounter, ever so gently. In a room already full of colour, a black and white zebra canvas restores a sense of calm; in a neutral interior, it adds character without ever shouting. This dialogue between black and white has inspired the very greatest: Victor Vasarely notably made it the subject of his painting Zebras (1937), often cited among the very first works of op art.

The colourful zebra, pop energy

Colour changes the mood entirely. The rainbow zebra unfolds a rich, painterly texture, while the multicoloured galloping zebra brings movement into the room. The perfect way to give a neutral living room the splash of colour it was missing. To carry this spirit further, explore our pop art wall art.

African and ethnic inspiration

For a warm interior in earthy tones, the zebra with tribal patterns and copper ochres brings its coppery hues to the wall. The African mother and child with zebra patterns, meanwhile, turns the stripe into clothing, in a tender illustration about what we hand down from one generation to the next. Two works that sit naturally alongside our African wall art; to style a whole room in this spirit, our guide to African decor gives you the keys.

Street art and watercolour, the zebra that makes you smile

The crowned elephant with zebra stripes blends graffiti with humour, for a loft, a home office or a teenager's bedroom that embraces its urban side. You will find more works in this style among our street art canvases. As for the laughing watercolour zebra, its soft tones bring a tender, joyful note to a child's room.

Zebra wall art for every room

In the living room, above the sofa

This is the prime spot. Aim for one artwork, or a pair, covering between half and two thirds of the width of the sofa, hung 15–25 cm (6–10 in) above the back. As a guide: a 60 × 80 cm (23.6 × 31.5 in) for a two-seater sofa, a 75 × 100 cm (29.5 × 39.4 in) for a three-seater, a 90 × 120 cm (35.4 × 47.2 in) for a large wall. Torn between a single piece and an arrangement? Two canvases side by side, or a trio in a row, make a beautiful gallery wall. More ideas among our living room wall art.

In the bedroom

Above the headboard, a black and white zebra canvas creates a hushed elegance, perfect for unwinding. The zebra in the snow, with its soft light, is a particularly lovely companion at the end of the day. Discover our bedroom wall art too.

In the entryway, hallway or home office

In an entryway, a portrait-format piece greets the eye from the doorway: it is the opening line of your home. In a home office, the clean lines of a black and white zebra structure the space without distracting, and make a beautiful backdrop for your video calls. Discover our entryway and hallway wall art and our home office wall art.

In a child's room

Children recognise the zebra at first glance. The laughing watercolour zebra brings softness, a rainbow zebra brings cheer, and a more graphic version will grow up alongside your child. More ideas in our children's room wall art.

What goes with zebra wall art?

The zebra's black and white are the ultimate neutrals. They pair with pale wood, linen, rattan, jute or cognac leather, and feel at home in a Scandinavian, Japandi, boho or industrial interior. For a safari-chic look, team it with green plants, a natural-fibre rug and a few touches of terracotta. Soft palettes suit it beautifully too: on a beige, sand or greige wall, its stripes take on magnificent depth. In the evening, low-angled light or a directional spotlight brings out the grain of the canvas.

The zebra also enjoys company. Surround it with other animals of the savannah, such as the lion in all its majesty (discover our lion artwork), or with its cousin the horse, with our horse paintings. For more inspiration, read our article how to decorate your home with animal art or our guide to Scandinavian style.

What the zebra symbolises

The zebra speaks of balance: black and white answer each other without ever fading away. It also speaks of individuality, since every zebra's stripes are unique, like a fingerprint. And as a herd animal, it evokes freedom lived together and our bonds with others.

In France, the zebra has also become the affectionate emblem of people with high intellectual potential (HPI), ever since the psychologist Jeanne Siaud-Facchin popularised the image: a singular being who blends into the background while standing out from it, and who will not be tamed. Giving a zebra painting to someone who recognises themselves in it is a tender, knowing wink.

Why does the zebra have stripes?

The question has intrigued naturalists since Darwin and Wallace. Several theories coexist: confusing predators' vision when the herd is on the move, helping to regulate heat and, according to the most recent studies, deterring biting flies. One thing is certain: this pattern, one of the most recognisable in the animal kingdom, is a gift to artists.

Sizes, finishes and frames

A painting is more than a printed image: it is a material you will look at every day for years. Here is what goes into ours.

  • 285 g/m² polyester canvas: a dense canvas with a subtly grained texture that captures the fine detail of the coat and the depth of the blacks.
  • High-pigment inks: rich, deep colours, guaranteed for 75 years without fading.
  • Solid wood stretcher: each canvas is stretched by hand, 3 cm (1.2 in) deep, for an elegant sense of depth.
  • Five edge finishes: White edges, Black edges, Gallery wrap, Mirrored edges or Folded edges, to dress the sides of the canvas just as you like.
  • Optional frame: white, matte black, antique silver, light oak or walnut, delivered assembled and ready to hang.
  • Sizes: from 30 × 40 to 90 × 120 cm (11.8 × 15.7 to 35.4 × 47.2 in), in portrait or landscape depending on the artwork, and up to 100 × 100 cm (39.4 × 39.4 in) for square pieces.

Need help with the size? Our guide how to choose the right size of wall art and our tips for hanging a picture safely will answer your questions. And to keep your canvas looking its best, here is how to care for your wall art.

Zebra canvas or zebra poster?

A canvas settles in as a centrepiece, made to last: it has texture, depth and a presence you feel the moment you walk into the room. A poster, a photo print on paper, is all about lightness and flexibility: ideal for a first decorating project, a gift or a wall you like to refresh. Several of our zebras come in both versions: discover our twin collection Zebra Posters & Prints.

Why choose MyselfMonArt?

Since 2022, more than 1,015 paintings have been unpacked in living rooms, bedrooms and hallways that were looking a little too bare. We do not try to offer everything: more than a thousand artworks have not made it past our art direction team, for the 700 in our collection today. Each canvas is designed in France, printed to order in Europe and shipped in reinforced packaging. Delivery is free, you have 14 days to change your mind, and you can pay in 3 interest-free instalments with Klarna on orders from €50. A question about a size? Our team in Toulouse will answer you on +33 9 60 44 61 50.

The zebra belongs to a large family: continue your visit with our animal wall art, the timeless elegance of black and white wall art or the patterns of our ethnic wall art.

With care, — Hayate & the MyselfMonArt team

Then choose the size according to the wall you want to dress.

faq.q: Black and white or colourful zebra wall art: which should I choose?

A colourful zebra, in a pop art spirit, becomes the burst of energy in a neutral interior or a child's room. A tip: echo one shade from the canvas in a cushion or a throw to create a real sense of harmony.

You can also line up two or three canvases of the same size for a gallery effect.

faq.q: What decor goes well with zebra wall art?
faq.a: The zebra's black and white pairs beautifully with pale wood, linen, rattan, jute or cognac leather. It feels at home in a Scandinavian, Japandi, boho or industrial interior, and reveals all its depth on a beige, sand or greige wall. For a safari-chic look, add green plants, a natural-fibre rug and a few touches of terracotta.

faq.q: What does the zebra symbolise in interior decor?

faq.q: Is zebra wall art suitable for a child's room?

posters-affiches-zebre.guide:
The zebra poster: stripes that transform a wall

A bare wall is more noticeable than you might think. Yet a single print is all it takes to bring it to life, and few animals do it as well as the zebra. Its stripes trace bold lines that guide the eye, and its black and white goes with almost everything. As a poster, this graphic quality takes on a lighter touch: you frame it in minutes, move it around, refresh it with the seasons, without ever giving up on elegance.

At MyselfMonArt, a creative studio founded in Toulouse in 2022, every image is selected and then retouched by hand by our art direction team: the contrasts, the light, the accuracy of the colours. Your poster is then printed to order, in high definition, on genuine photo paper, edge to edge, for a crisp, luminous full-bleed finish.

What does the zebra symbolise?

If the zebra is so loved in interior decor, it is also because of the story it tells. Its black and white stripes balance each other without ever fading away. They are unique to each animal, like a signature. And this great traveller of the savannah lives in a herd, an image of shared freedom. A zebra print is a little of that harmony of opposites hanging on your wall, and an invitation to travel.

Which zebra poster should you choose?

The black and white zebra print, photographic elegance

Black and white never goes out of style, and nothing shows off the pattern better. The wild gaze in black and white draws you into the heart of the coat, in a striking face-to-face. The zebra in the snow captures a moment of winter held in suspense. And the intimate portrait with golden stripes emerges in chiaroscuro against a black background. In a room full of colour, a black and white zebra poster gives the eye a place to rest; in a pared-back setting, it becomes the wall's signature. This optical play also inspired Victor Vasarely, whose painting Zebras (1937) is often described as one of the very first works of op art. It sits naturally alongside our other black and white posters.

Colour, for pop energy

Colour, meanwhile, brings a breath of pop. The rainbow zebra unrolls multicoloured stripes full of energy, waking up a white wall and a child's room alike. To carry this spirit further, discover our pop art posters.

African spirit, for graphic warmth

The zebra with tribal patterns and copper ochres warms the wall with its earthy tones, while the African mother and child with zebra patterns turns the stripe into clothing, in a tender, graphic illustration. Pair them with our African posters and prints, and draw styling ideas from our guide to African decor.

Framing your zebra print

You have two options. Choose No frame and you receive the print on its own, ready to slip into a standard shop-bought frame of the same size, or into a made-to-measure frame for larger sizes: slim and black for a gallery look, pale wood for a softer feel. Choose With frame and it arrives ready to hang, in four finishes: white, matte black, light oak or walnut, in 30 × 40, 60 × 80 or 75 × 100 cm (11.8 × 15.7, 23.6 × 31.5 or 29.5 × 39.4 in). The White border option adds a margin around the image, much like a mount: the stripes have room to breathe and the whole piece gains in refinement.

Prefer an artist's-studio feel, with no frame at all? A print can also hang between two wooden poster hangers, or from discreet clips on a taut wire. For a large size, spread the hanging points evenly: our tips for hanging safely will help.

Where should you hang a zebra poster?

  • In the living room: above the sofa, aim for a print, or an arrangement, covering between half and two thirds of the width of the furniture. A 75 × 100 or 90 × 120 cm (29.5 × 39.4 or 35.4 × 47.2 in) makes a real statement. More ideas among our living room posters.
  • In the bedroom: a black and white version above the headboard brings a hushed elegance, perfect for calm. Discover our bedroom posters.
  • In a child's room: children recognise the zebra at first glance. The rainbow print or the tender African mother and child feel right at home there, as do our kids' room posters.
  • In the entryway or hallway: a portrait format sets the tone from the doorway. Discover our entryway and hallway posters.
  • In the home office: the clean lines of a black and white zebra structure the space without distracting. Discover our office posters.
  • In a bathroom or toilet: the little graphic touch, with a dash of humour, that takes everyone by surprise. Choose a well-ventilated wall, away from water splashes.

To find the right size, the pointers in our guide how to choose the right size of wall art apply to posters too.

Creating a gallery wall around the zebra

Posters are made for gallery walls. Start with a zebra print as the centrepiece, then surround it with pieces that echo it: other animals of the savannah, such as the lion poster, nature prints or black and white images. Three rules are all you need:

  • a common thread: the palette (black, white, ochre) or the theme (the savannah);
  • one family of frames, or two finishes that complement each other, such as matte black and light oak;
  • even spacing, 5–8 cm (2–3 in) between each print.

Lay your prints out on the floor first to find the right balance. A symmetrical pair above a bed, a trio in a row above a sofa or a grid of six prints on a large wall: the scale is yours to choose.

Zebra poster or canvas?

A poster is all about flexibility: a light, affordable photo print, ideal for a first decorating project, a gift, a rental or a wall you like to keep evolving. A canvas, stretched by hand over a solid wood stretcher, settles in as a centrepiece made to last, with the texture and depth of a true artwork. One does not rule out the other: they are two ways of bringing a wall to life. Several of our zebras come in both versions: find them in our Zebra Artwork collection.

Why choose MyselfMonArt?

Our art direction team turns away more images than it keeps: more than a thousand have not made it through, for the 700 artworks in our collection today. Each poster is then printed for you, to order, in Europe, and shipped with care. Free delivery, 14 days to change your mind, and payment in 3 interest-free instalments with Klarna on orders from €50: everything is designed so you can choose with peace of mind. Unsure about a size or a frame? Call us on +33 9 60 44 61 50: a real person from our Toulouse team will advise you.

Ready to take the journey further? Explore our animal posters and prints, the elegance of the horse poster or our full range of posters and art prints. And for more ideas, read our article how to decorate your home with animal art.

With care, — Hayate & the MyselfMonArt team

faq.q: What does the zebra symbolise in interior decor?
faq.a: The zebra symbolises balance, as its black and white stripes answer each other without fading away, and individuality: every zebra's stripes are unique, like a fingerprint. As a herd animal, it also evokes freedom and our bonds with others. In interior decor, a zebra print brings a soothing graphic contrast and a hint of escape to the African savannah, while remaining very easy to work into any space.

faq.q: Zebra poster or canvas: which should I choose?
faq.a: Choose a poster for flexibility: a light, affordable photo print that is easy to frame and to change whenever you like. Opt for a canvas for a lasting centrepiece, stretched by hand over a solid wood stretcher. Several of our zebras are available in both versions: find the canvases in our Zebra Artwork collection.

faq.q: How should I frame a zebra print?
faq.a: Choose “No frame” and the print slips into a standard shop-bought frame of the same size, or into a made-to-measure frame for larger sizes. Choose “With frame” and it arrives ready to hang, in white, matte black, light oak or walnut, from 30 × 40 to 75 × 100 cm (11.8 × 15.7 to 29.5 × 39.4 in). The “White border” option adds a margin around the image, much like a mount, for a gallery effect that lets the stripes breathe.

faq.q: How can I hang a poster on the wall without a frame?
faq.a: For an artist's-studio feel, hang your print between two wooden poster hangers, or attach it with discreet clips on a taut wire. These solutions do not pierce the paper and make it easy to swap prints. For a crisper, longer-lasting result, especially in a large size, framing remains the best option.

faq.q: What size zebra poster should I choose?
faq.a: Our prints come in 30 × 40, 60 × 80, 75 × 100 and 90 × 120 cm (11.8 × 15.7, 23.6 × 31.5, 29.5 × 39.4 and 35.4 × 47.2 in). Aim for between half and two thirds of the width of the furniture you are hanging it above: a 75 × 100 or 90 × 120 cm (29.5 × 39.4 or 35.4 × 47.2 in) above a sofa, a 60 × 80 cm (23.6 × 31.5 in) above a console table. The 30 × 40 cm (11.8 × 15.7 in) is ideal in a gallery wall. Not sure? Cut a piece of cardboard to size and hold it against the wall.

faq.q: Is a zebra print suitable for a child's room?
faq.a: Yes, all the more so as children recognise the zebra at first glance. The rainbow zebra brings cheer, the African mother and child with zebra patterns a tender softness, and a black and white version will grow up alongside your child. Pair it with other savannah animals to create a little safari on the wall. More ideas in our kids' room posters.

faq.q: Can I hang a zebra print in a bathroom?
faq.a: Yes, it is even an original way to bring a graphic touch and a dash of humour to a bathroom or a downstairs loo. As with any paper print, choose a well-ventilated wall, away from water splashes and direct steam from the shower. The “With frame” option gives a crisper, more polished result in these smaller rooms.

faq.a: Each print is produced to order in high definition on genuine photo paper, edge to edge for a full-bleed finish. Colours are vibrant and true, details sharp, bringing out the fine lines of the stripes.
